title: When the Witness Wakes
premise: Cyrus Iversen, a reclusive insurance investigator whose photographic memory has quietly exposed three 'accidental' deaths as murders, is pulled into a fourth case when a drowned woman is found wearing clothes stolen from his own closet—clothes only someone inside his life could have taken. As he investigates, he realizes the killer is mirroring the details of his three previous cases, someone with access to his private case files and a grudge tied to a death he failed to prevent years ago. The killer is Marta Voss, the sister of a man whose wrongful death Cyrus once helped bury in paperwork, and she intends to make him the final victim of a staged accident. In the end, Cyrus chooses to break his own rules, testifying publicly about the covered-up death and trading his invisibility for justice, while the found family he never meant to build helps him survive her trap.
about_author: Lena Ravensworth is the pen name of a former claims adjuster who spent eleven years reading other people's disasters before writing about them. She lives in a coastal town where fog is frequent and bodies are, thankfully, fictional.

chapters.title: The Fourth Body
chapters.summary: Cyrus Iversen's POV. Called to assess a drowning claim, Cyrus recognizes the victim's outfit instantly—it's his, stolen from his closet while he slept. The police see coincidence; his memory sees staging. Emotional beat: cold dread as the boundary between his hidden work and his private life collapses for the first time.

chapters.title: A Memory of Everything
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, with flashbacks to the three deaths he quietly solved. He reviews his mental archive of each case, hunting for what connects them to this new victim, Dana Kellerman—a night nurse who once treated one of his earlier subjects. Emotional beat: the loneliness of a mind that forgets nothing and trusts no one.

chapters.title: The Neighbor Who Knocks
chapters.summary: Alternating POV introducing Odile Brant, a retired forensic photographer who lives upstairs and refuses to be ignored. She notices Cyrus's sleeplessness and inserts herself into the investigation uninvited. Emotional beat: reluctant warmth—the first crack in Cyrus's isolation as Odile reads details off crime scene photos he missed.

chapters.title: Stolen Hours
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. He reconstructs the theft from his apartment: no forced entry, no memory of disturbance, meaning the killer was someone he let close or someone who studied him long enough to move unseen. A copy of his old case file surfaces at a used bookstore, annotated in unfamiliar handwriting. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening into obsession.

chapters.title: What the File Forgot
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She digs into the annotated file and finds a name redacted from every version: Elias Voss, a warehouse worker whose death Cyrus's report helped classify as accidental eight years ago. Emotional beat: dawning horror that Cyrus's careful work may have once buried an innocent man.

chapters.title: The Sister
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. He tracks Marta Voss, Elias's sister, now a hospice administrator who had access to Dana Kellerman and to the archive where his files were stored. Their first conversation is polite, grief-edged, and full of traps he only half-sees. Emotional beat: guilt meeting charm, and losing.

chapters.title: Accident, Rehearsed
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A near-fatal gas leak in Cyrus's building mirrors the exact method of Elias Voss's death; Odile realizes Marta isn't just killing—she's restaging the old case with Cyrus cast as the corpse. They go to the police, who find nothing actionable. Emotional beat: fury at a system that requires a body before it believes.

chapters.title: The Confession Trap
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Out of legal options, Cyrus decides to bait Marta: he leaks that he's reopening the Voss file and will announce his findings at the harbor warehouse where Elias died. Odile rigs the space with cameras; a young claims clerk, Theo, insists on helping despite the risk. Emotional beat: terrified resolve—found family forming under fire.

chapters.title: Where Elias Died
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, climax. Marta comes not to confess but to finish the restaging, and Cyrus confronts her with the one thing her plan couldn't anticipate: his public, on-camera testimony about what really happened to her brother, including his own complicity. She falters between vengeance and being heard; Odile and Theo intervene before either wins. Emotional beat: catharsis through surrender of control.

chapters.title: The Witness Wakes
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, resolution. Marta is arrested; Cyrus's testimony forces a formal inquiry into the Voss death and two others like it. His anonymity is gone, but so is the weight he carried alone—Odile and Theo become the family he stopped pretending not to want. Final beat: he opens a new case file, no longer invisible, no longer alone.
